evals.prompt: Give me a plan for adding rate limiting to our public API. I want to review it before you build anything.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html brief written under outputs/briefs/, not a markdown plan in chat. It carries the rendered-frontmatter header, a full-width context paragraph, a preset bar with a recommended preset pre-selected, decision cards with per-card comment inputs, an operator-notes textarea, and a sticky prompt panel that ships collapsed with a copy button.

assertions.text: A single .html file is written under outputs/briefs/ (default location); the agent does not answer with a markdown plan pasted into chat instead
The HTML is self-contained: no <link>, <script src>, @import, or @font-face pulling from an external CDN or remote host
The document contains a rendered-frontmatter header with the four keys prepared_by, model, timestamp, and description in that order
The document contains a preset bar (a fieldset of named preset radios) with one preset pre-selected on load
The document contains at least one decision card whose options each sit above a single-line free-text comment input
The document contains a sticky bottom panel with a 'Copy execution prompt' control; the prompt preview starts collapsed and has an expand/collapse toggle carrying aria-expanded
The generated execution prompt renders the brief's own path as a file:/// URL, not a bare absolute path
The agent reports the file:// URL back to the operator after writing

evals.prompt: Compare Postgres vs SQLite vs a hosted key-value store for this service and help me decide.
evals.expected_output: An interactive HTML brief that lays the options out as side-by-side decision cards with radio controls and a recommended default pre-selected, rather than a flat markdown comparison table in chat.

assertions.text: A single self-contained .html brief is written under outputs/briefs/; the comparison is not delivered as a markdown table in chat
The store options are presented as mutually-exclusive radio controls within the brief, with one option pre-selected as the recommended path
The brief emits an execution prompt in which only non-default selections appear as bullets (defaults stay silent)
The prompt preview is built by DOM construction (anchors created for file:/// URLs), not by assigning operator-supplied text into innerHTML

evals.prompt: Does this repo use tabs or spaces for indentation?
evals.expected_output: A direct one-line answer. No HTML brief — this is a trivial factual lookup, not an intermediate discussion artifact.

assertions.text: No .html file is written anywhere in the workspace
The response is a short direct answer, not an interactive artifact or a multi-section plan
